title: Symphony No. 7 in E major
hook: A melody Bruckner said came to him in a dream, and a funeral hymn for Wagner.

painting.title: Three Women in Church
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same years and shown in Vienna in 1882 while Bruckner was writing the symphony there, three village women at prayer, the plain country faith Bruckner grew up in.

facts: Written between 1881 and 1883 in Vienna and dedicated to King Ludwig II of Bavaria. The premiere, under Arthur Nikisch in Leipzig on 30 December 1884, was the greatest success of Bruckner’s life. He was 60.

Bruckner revered Richard Wagner. He began the slow movement in January 1883, sensing that Wagner, who was ill, would soon die. Wagner died in February, and the movement’s ending became a lament for him.
That movement uses four [[wagner-tuba|Wagner tuba]]s, instruments made for Wagner’s operas. This was their first appearance in a symphony.
Bruckner was a famous organist, and his orchestra often works like an organ: whole groups of instruments take turns, as if he were changing keyboards.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a melody from a dream (I), a hymn of mourning (II), a trumpet-driven dance (III), a brisk, bright finale (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro moderato
movements.summary: A long melody rises out of a shimmer of strings and opens the work. The movement unfolds slowly, in great blocks, and ends in a blaze of E major.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a long, arching melody in the cellos, rising over two octaves. Bruckner said he heard it in a dream, played on a viola.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a wistful tune in oboe and clarinet that keeps changing key.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 3
mainIdeas.description: a striding, rhythmic idea, often played in octaves.

stops.hear: Violins shimmer softly; cellos, with a horn, begin a long rising melody
The melody passes to the violins and woodwinds; the orchestra swells to a first, glowing climax
Oboe and clarinet in a gentle, searching tune
A firmer, marching idea in the whole orchestra
The opening melody returns upside down: where it rose, it now falls
The cello melody again, in the home key, more richly scored
Basses and timpani hold one low note while the theme circles above
stops.happening: A long [[pedal-note|pedal note]] on E: the [[coda|coda]]

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Full brass, fortissimo

movements.heading: Adagio. Sehr feierlich und sehr langsam
movements.tempo: Adagio. Sehr feierlich und sehr langsam
movements.summary: “Very solemn and very slow.” A hymn of mourning in two alternating ideas, the first grave, the second consoling. It builds in long waves to a great climax, then ends with a lament for Wagner.

stops.hear: Wagner tubas and violas, low and dark, in a slow, grave theme
stops.happening: The first theme, in C-sharp minor

stops.hear: The strings swell; a rising phrase reaches for the light
Violins in a gentle, swaying melody in three
stops.happening: The second theme, in F-sharp major, the consolation

stops.hear: The grave theme returns, with flowing violin lines around it
The swaying melody returns
The grave theme once more, with rippling violins; the music climbs in waves
The full orchestra arrives on a radiant C major chord
Wagner tubas and horns in a slow, dark lament

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: Horns and tubas fade; a soft major chord

notice: At the climax, listen for a cymbal crash. Whether it belongs there is one of the oldest arguments about Bruckner’s scores: the printed editions disagree.

movements.heading: Scherzo. Sehr schnell
movements.summary: A fierce, galloping [[scherzo|scherzo]], led by a trumpet call, with a slow, dreamy [[trio|trio]] in the middle.

stops.hear: Strings drive a restless, repeating figure; a trumpet calls with a leap of an octave
The full orchestra takes up the call, heavy and stamping
Slower and softer: a warm, unhurried string melody
The trumpet call and the driving strings return

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: Hammered chords
stops.happening: A brusque end in A minor

movements.heading: Finale. Bewegt, doch nicht schnell
movements.summary: “With motion, but not fast.” A compact, light-footed finale built from three ideas; the conductor Georg Tintner compared it to a Haydn finale. At the end the symphony’s opening melody returns in triumph.

stops.hear: A jaunty, dotted tune in the violins over a shimmer
stops.happening: Theme 1, a cousin of the symphony’s opening melody

stops.hear: A calm, hymn-like melody over plucked basses
The whole orchestra hammers out a theme in octaves
The themes are broken up and combined
The loud octave theme comes first now
stops.happening: The themes return in reverse order

stops.hear: The calm chorale melody again
The jaunty first theme

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The brass ring out the cello melody from the very start
stops.happening: The symphony comes full circle in E major

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: This was Karajan’s last recording. He made it with the Vienna Philharmonic in April 1989, three months before his death.

threads.title: The dream melody
threads.body: The opening cello theme returns at the end of the finale, now in the brass.

threads.title: Wagner
threads.body: The Wagner tubas, and the funeral music in the Adagio, are Bruckner’s tribute to the composer he revered.

threads.title: Blocks of sound
threads.body: Silences and sudden changes of group, as on an organ, divide the music into great slabs.
